loop: gauntlet: a builder and a separate critic with fresh context per piece. The critic runs ours next to native, names the biggest gap, and the piece loops until the critic picks ours.
bar: native APFS (this Mac) and ext4 (moonscape): cargo build and git status within 1.5x, pjdfstest + fsx + xfstests-generic no worse than native, zero data loss in crash-injection.

items.title: #1 dedup ratio on the real worktree corpus
items.detail: Full run on 45 slots, 843,889 files, 273.43 GiB raw, 0 errors. Raw 1.00x, per-file zstd 3.60x, whole-file dedup 3.12x, CDC only 5.08x, CDC + zstd 14.04x. A median extra lumen slot costs 0.47 GiB compressed (4.9% of raw). Caveat: 97.5% of raw is cargo target/ and 91.7% is one repo, so 14x is a Rust build-output result. Write-up: docs/spikes/1-dedup-corpus.md. Gate met.

items.title: #2 mmap and file locking over the macOS NFS loopback
items.detail: Viable without sudo (-o locallocks). 24/24 checks. Tuned server: clean builds 0.9x-1.2x native, git status 1.3x-1.4x, warm and incremental builds 2.5x-3.5x (misses 1.5x, see #18). Old server was 3-5x clean and 9-55x warm because of nfsserve bugs (LINK, tracker lock, readdir cookie), fixed in the vendored copy (#19). One 60-dep crate, passthrough server, n=3-5. items.title: #4 .git inside the filesystem

items.title: #5 treehouse process detection on the mount
items.detail: cwd-only detection works on the mount for every detectable case. Gap: a process holding an open fd or flock after chdir out is not detected, and on the mount the reset leaves a .nfs silly-rename file and a dirty slot while return exits 0 (#20). lsof and cwd lookup fine. items.title: #6 artifact byte-identity across slots at different paths
items.detail: Independent debug slots cost 12.8%-28% of slot 1 after dedup, 1.8% release. Remapping or CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 brings it under 3%. Clone-seeded plus one edit: 8.8%-10.3%. Slot-specific remap makes a copied target dirty. Mount namespaces (#17) not needed for dedup on these crates. Two small crates, one run per cell. docs/spikes/6-artifact-byte-identity.md

items.title: #18 decision: warm and incremental builds 2.5x-3.5x over NFS loopback
items.detail: Option 1 experiment done (docs/spikes/2-nfs-loopback.md, Spike 18): a rebuild is ~9,600 NFS ops (4,300 LOOKUP), not 20,000. Best config cuts ops (X edit 9,611 to 5,683) and wall ratio to ~2-4x, but 91% of 1,073 runs were at load > 30 so ratios are indicative only; no cell is convincingly within 1.5x. Remaining ~1,100-1,400 misses are negative entries the client drops when rustc changes directory mtime (macOS client). Recommendation: take option 3 (reframe criterion 2 for macOS warm builds), adopt AppleDouble translation, a readdir cache with cookie verifier and the SETATTR guard fix in v1. Needs your decision.

items.title: #7 chunking, hashing and block store
items.detail: Round 1 F1-F10 fixed and held (1800 simulated power-loss cases: 0 acked blocks lost, 0 wrong bytes; 3 min 8-thread stress 27.7M ops, 0 errors; builds on Rust 1.89). Round 2 verdict: NOT mergeable. N1: a benign torn write becomes permanent 'corruption' after the next sync moves the watermark over the gap (about 7% of simulated crashes), and cowfs-core refuses to mount on it. N2: watermark ahead of the packs makes sync() silently stop fsyncing. N3: a deleted middle pack is not reported. N4: a failed pack roll wedges puts forever (AlreadyExists). N5: the 64 MiB resync budget can drop a whole damaged pack from the index (1100 damaged records lost all 4095 blocks, ~3000 valid). Also 8 real mutant gaps. Builder fixing (header CRC format change, torn-tail sidecar, transactional roll, pack manifest, salvage API).

items.title: #8 Merkle tree and O(1) writable snapshots
items.detail: Critic verdict: NOT mergeable. Tree, refcounts and crash atomicity held against a harsher harness (reordering, 512 B/4 KiB tearing, every-event crash, snapshot-remove crash). Blockers: F1 before_sync hook runs BEFORE the closure so a put-then-set_content batch made durable metadata reference unsynced blocks in 10 of 30 commits; F2 clean drop makes metadata durable even when the hook fails; F3 inode numbers are reused after a crash (100 creates, crash, next ino 2), aliasing stale handles. Also: no flush timer, lost fsync makes the file unopenable (fails closed), lookup 39 us at 1M, 1.7 ms per unbatched op, remove_snapshot stalls writers 837 ms, no magic check, 4 mutants survive. Builder fixing with API changes for core listed in docs/v1-meta.md.

items.detail: Critic verdict: NOT mergeable. Tree, refcounts and crash atomicity held against a harsher harness (reordering, 512 B/4 KiB tearing, every-event crash, snapshot-remove crash). items.title: #10 garbage collection
#11 Linux FUSE mount
items.detail: Critic verdict: NOT mergeable. Blockers: (1) 3600 s ttl + keep_cache leaves changes behind the mount invisible for up to an hour and caused silent data corruption (O_APPEND at a stale size overwrote data); nothing wires the invalidate API and the kernel ignores negative-entry invalidation (verified on 7.0). (2) A Vfs panic hangs the read and the mount vanishes with no error. (3) Single-threaded loop: one 1 s read delayed a stat 852 ms; 4 readers at 100 ms gave lookup p50 835 ms. Also SIGTERM leaves the mount, 8 of 21 mutants survive, inode reuse untested. Passed: 15/15 mount tests, fsx 1e5 ops x2, git/tar/cp/mmap, race test, forget accounting, latency floor reproduces. Builder fixing: short default ttl, opt-in SoleWriter with an Invalidator, catch_unwind, keyed-lane worker pool.

items.title: #12 macOS NFS loopback mount
items.detail: Round-1 findings fixed with regression tests (I re-ran: 38 nfsserve/adapter + protocol tests pass, fmt/clippy clean, CI green): reference-balance leak, AppleDouble Translate (sidecar to xattrs, no sidecar inodes; 200 files = 200 inodes vs 400), one-shot MNT + keyed MAC handles + generations, DoS bounds, retransmission reply cache, inode-reuse STALE, signal cleanup + stale-mount sweep. Mutants 21/22 killed. Caveats: latency at load 42-65 (inline_metadata helps writes and reads, noisy), no before/after RPC baseline, lsof peer-uid check adds almost nothing, RSS soak 3 to 40 MiB unexplained, real files named ._x invisible under Translate. Translate is new stateful code, so a round-2 critic is attacking it.

items.title: #13 CLI and Unix-socket control API
items.detail: Critic findings fixed, re-verified. Linux CI failure fixed: connecting to a regular file gives ECONNREFUSED on Linux and ENOTSOCK on macOS; exit 3 now means missing path or a socket that refuses, exit 1 for a path that is not a socket. Full suite passes in the Linux VM, first Linux run of SO_PEERCRED. Decisions for lead: snapshot_reset/busy semantics, name rules vs core, import hash scope. Not built: real backend (seam only), no TTY test.

#29 cowfs-vfs trait, MemVfs and conformance suite
items.detail: Critic findings fixed and re-verified by me: 127 checks tagged Posix/Portable/Cowfs, Options::skip with reasons shown in the report, oracle precedence fixed, 57 faults all caught (full release run 62 s, passes), default crate tests about 20 s, no flakes in 20 runs or under 8 CPU burners (builder's numbers). Not done: oracle does not check timestamps, blocks, xattr flags or short reads (direct checks cover them). The Posix level is unverified on native filesystems until #34 runs it. Needs a CI job for the feature-gated full mutation run.

items.title: #26 cowfs-core: Vfs over store and meta
items.detail: Builder done, re-verified by me: 127 conformance checks pass through Core (2 heavy separately), 18 core tests, model proptests, crash images 280 and kill -9 120 rounds with 0 failures, negative control finds a dangling chunk. Benchmarks at load 54-111: lookups at or above native (miss 2.7M/s vs 460k/s), data 6-57x slower than APFS page cache (seq read 637 MiB/s, write 239), snapshot create 12-21 ms at 100k files. Core refuses to open a store with corrupt_synced. Open: virtual-inode alias table, chunk lists loaded whole (splice_content unused), flush() does nothing, snapshot rename/promote not atomic (needs Meta::rename_snapshot), batch timestamps, ChunkRef hole flag, early ino reservation. Critic attacking durability ordering, write-back semantics, partial chunks, ino reuse, caches, concurrency and mutants.

items.title: #34 cowfs-vfs-path: run the suite on native filesystems and through mounts
items.detail: PathVfs built; suite ran on APFS (99/114), case-sensitive APFS (99), btrfs (100), ext4 (112), FUSE (112, same 2 failures as native ext4, so no FUSE adapter bug), NFS (88, 26 fail). No adapter bug confirmed; 12 NFS failures are the client's silly rename (.nfs.* files), 1 is RENAME_EXCL ENOTSUP. Suite bugs found: dir nlink formula, symlink xattrs, 60 kB xattr, 4095-byte symlink targets, and concurrent read/write shows torn reads natively on ext4 and btrfs (6 of 10 runs). Silly rename makes unlink-while-open, forget and rmdir-while-referenced unjudgeable through NFS: now being run at protocol level. Builder is fixing Linux clippy, merging the revised suite and rerunning the matrix at Posix level.
